column1: # How a family's act is counted: arms in order, the first whose selector holds deciding. Applied by tools/build_family_model.py as the `count` cell.
# selector: `*` (every row of the family) or tests joined by " & ", each key=value|value. Keys: leaf, verb, identity, group, seats.
# doors: none (one signature carries the row) | shut | ROW[@source][!confers|!result], ROW a row of constitution/governance_policy.tsv.
# source (whose roster the row is read against): subject_group | signer_group | dimension_authority | accord | trust_root | self | conferrer.
# The quote must stand verbatim in the cited section. A family whose cosign cell reads none and has no row here counts `none`.

column5: quote
The first three are single-signer (below)
a resignation is signed by the leaving member
is admitted only when countersigned by a key outside the deciding seat
a widening or removal is cosigned under the group's `consensus_protocol`
One holder can stop every agent instantly and silently
unless a strict majority of the standing roster confirms it
It is a cosigned row by a strict majority of the standing roster
The door is a person's: it governs the roster of a user fedID.
an agent's occurrence is single-signer, and neither runs these paths
for an occurrence of a `node` or `agent` identity, which is single-signer in any case
for an occurrence of a user self only when cosigned by a **strict majority of the self's current live roster**
There is **one ballot per person** however many keys they hold
the winner's acceptance row binds the ballot set it was seated on
That act is the governance table's `custodian_replace` row
one cosigned `retirement:custodian_minted:v1` row
On their absence, the community vote carries.
a signed, roster-pinned vote on a pending act
**Neither row is the event.**
